metadata.title: Raymond James bullish on Schwab amid ‘compelling valuation’

content.text:
Investing.com -- Raymond James upgraded Charles Schwab (NYSE:SCHW) to Strong Buy with a $135 price target in a note on Wednesday, telling investors that the brokerage is a clear winner from interest rates staying higher for longer.
"We view Schwab as a clear beneficiary from higher-for-longer interest rates which should drive continued healthy net interest margin expansion," analyst Patrick O'Shaughnessy wrote.
Schwab's net interest margin, a key measure of profit from lending and deposits, rose to 3.04% in the third quarter from 2.88% a year earlier. Raymond James expects it to climb toward the mid-3% range in 2027 and the high-3% range by 2028.
The firm also pointed to healthy growth in Schwab's core business. Account growth accelerated to 6%, matching Robinhood despite Schwab's much larger customer base, and net new assets hit a record in the third quarter.
Bank lending is also growing quickly, with balances on loans backed by clients' investment portfolios up nearly 60% year over year. Lending now makes up 8% of net revenue, up from 3% two years ago.
O'Shaughnessy dismissed concerns that AI agents will help customers move idle cash out of low-yielding Schwab accounts into higher-paying alternatives, a process known as cash sorting.
"We view the bear case regarding agentic AI-driven cash sorting as substantially overdone and providing a very attractive entry point with Schwab's shares trading at just 11.5x our above-consensus 2027 EPS estimate," he said.
Raymond James expects Schwab to deliver EPS growth of more than 20% in 2027 and more than 15% in 2028. Its 2027 EPS estimate of $8.05 is above the $7.86 consensus.
